validate_dacl.postcondition: On return 0: all ACEs within pdacl have been walked and each ACE's size and sid.num_subauth are within [pdacl, end_of_acl]; subsequent traversal of the DACL is safe. Findings about pointer arithmetic or struct field accesses INSIDE validate_dacl() are part of the validation logic, not vulnerable sinks.

validate_t2.postcondition: On return 0: if min_param_size > 0, ParameterOffset + min_param_size <= frame_end (actual received packet end); if min_data_size > 0, DataOffset + min_data_size <= frame_end. A caller that passes sizeof(struct) as min_data_size can safely dereference that struct at DataOffset. Passing 0 for one skips its size check but both offsets are still bounded by CIFSMaxBufSize + MAX_CIFS_HDR_SIZE.

smb2_validate_iov.postcondition: On return 0: offset + sizeof_hdr fits within the iov and the actual response length >= min_len; the struct pointer derived by adding offset to the iov base is within the received buffer.

smb2_validate_and_copy_iov.postcondition: On return 0: calls smb2_validate_iov (same postcondition), then copies the validated region to a fresh buffer; the returned pointer and length are safe to dereference up to min_len bytes.

dacl_offset_valid.postcondition: On return true (non-zero): the DACL pointer derived from acl_base + le32_to_cpu(dacl_off) is within [acl_base, end_of_acl] with at least sizeof(smb_acl) bytes remaining; safe to pass to validate_dacl().

sid_to_id.postcondition: On return 0, psid->num_subauth has been verified to be <= SID_MAX_SUB_AUTHORITIES (making the psid subauthority array safe to access), and sidkey->datalen has been verified to equal sizeof(uid_t) before any memcpy from the key payload, ensuring the payload copy is bounds-safe.
